defs: Transforms readable plaintext into ciphertext using an algorithm and key so unauthorized parties cannot understand it.
A control that permits or blocks network traffic according to configured rules.

course.learn: Hardening reduces attack surface by disabling unnecessary services, closing unused ports, removing unused software/accounts, changing defaults, enforcing secure configuration, patching, and enabling appropriate protections.
course.why: Every unnecessary feature is another component that can fail or be attacked.
course.example: A new server is built from a secure baseline: unused packages removed, SSH restricted, default accounts disabled, logging enabled, and patches applied.
course.exam: Hardening = reduce exposure and insecure defaults. Baselines help keep hardening consistent.
